bottom_line: Stocks bounced hard this week after a November sell-off pushed the S&P 500 into a correction. Under the bounce, the big worry is unchanged: inflation is high, and the chances that the Fed (the people who set interest rates) raises rates are going up.

stories.title: Stocks bounce after a rough November
stories.real: On a short Black Friday session the Dow jumped 510 points, the S&P 500 rose 1.2% and the Nasdaq gained 1.7%, putting the S&P on track for its best week since April 2025. This came after a November sell-off had dragged the S&P 500 into a correction, which means a drop of 10% or more from its high.
stories.you: If you own index funds in a retirement account, part of this month's loss came back this week, but one good week doesn't undo a correction.

stories.real: Inflation hit a 3-year high, and the chances of a Fed rate hike are rising. Next week's jobs report is the next big test before the Fed's December rate decision.
stories.you: If the Fed raises rates, credit card, car loan and home loan rates usually go up with it.

stories.title: Big-ticket stuff costs a lot
stories.real: The 30-year fixed mortgage averages 7.21%, and buyers are switching to adjustable loans to get a lower starting payment. The average new car price hit a record $51,109 in October, and rising prices are squeezing holiday budgets.
stories.you: Adjustable loans can cost more later if rates rise, so know how high your payment could go before you sign.

stories.title: Trump attacks GDP number
stories.real: The government revised its third-quarter GDP number (the total size of the economy's output) massively higher. President Trump called the revision a 'record setting error' and demanded an immediate investigation.
stories.you: Fights over official numbers make it harder for everyone, including the Fed, to agree on how the economy is really doing.

stories.real: Jensen Huang returned as Nvidia's CEO after a shock leadership shake-up. Chip stocks led the Black Friday rally, but Nvidia missed out and is still paying the price for the drama.
stories.you: Nvidia is a huge piece of many index funds and Asian markets, so turmoil at one company can move a lot of people's savings.
